title: Reverse Vowels of a String
summary: Given a string s, reverse the order of all vowels within it while keeping other characters unchanged, and return the modified string.
statement: Given a string s, reverse the order of all vowels within it while keeping other characters unchanged, and return the modified string. The vowels considered are 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', and 'u', including both lowercase and uppercase forms.
constraints: 1 <= len(s) <= 300000; all characters are printable ASCII (codes 32–126).
Reverse only the occurrences of a,e,i,o,u and A,E,I,O,U. Every non-vowel stays at its original index; each vowel keeps its own case when it moves.
hints: Only positions holding vowels may change.
Move a left and right pointer past non-vowels, then swap the two vowel characters.
Convert to a character list. Seek the next vowel at each end, swap them, move inward, and finally join the list.
Use both uppercase and lowercase vowels in the membership set, and move the complete character without changing its case.
editorial: The leftmost vowel belongs at the rightmost vowel position and vice versa. Scanning past consonants preserves their positions, while swapping only vowels reverses that subsequence. Python strings are immutable, so the character list and output require linear space. The oracle independently extracts all vowels and refills vowel positions from the reversed extraction.

tests.explanation: The vowel sequence I,e,e,A reverses to A,e,e,I, producing AceCreIm. Consonant positions are unchanged.
Vowels e,e,o,e reverse to e,o,e,e, producing leotcede.
